title: Sixteen
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies (the trilogy ran in print in three papers)
logline: Friday. The vet. The word 'sixteen' said aloud by someone who isn't Wood. The strip draws the vet's mouth and nothing else of her. The dog's paw on Wood's hand: the reverse of the hand-on-the-dog panels.

panels.composition: The vet's steel table. BARNABY on it. WOOD's hands either side. A VET drawn as a white coat and a mouth.

balloons.text: Sixteen. He's sixteen, Arthur. Everything he does now is a gift.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, an old dog on a vet's steel table between a thin man's hands, a vet visible only as a white coat and a speaking mouth
image.notes: The vet says 'Arthur.' The strip lets strangers say it; friends don't.

panels.composition: The dog's paw on Wood's hand. Not the reverse.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, close-up of an old dog's paw resting on a man's hand on a steel table, no words
image.notes: The reverse of the hand-on-the-dog panels. The dog's paw, on him.

panels.composition: Wood not saying anything. The vet's mouth, closed now. The dog looking at the door.

image.prompt: quiet ink line with water bleeding over the edges, desaturated wet-on-wet in raw umber and Payne's gray and Prussian blue, a thin man silent at a vet's table with an old dog looking toward the door, no words

panels.composition: The Legacy in the lot. The dog on the passenger seat. Wood's hand on the gearshift. The dog's chin on his wrist. The word not in the panel.
